newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana's Home Finance Company plans new bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Ghana's Home Finance Company plans new bond issue.

text.p: Ghana's main mortgage lender, Home Finance Company, will offer a second tranche of its successful U.S. dollar-indexed corporate bonds before the end of July, its finance director said on Thursday.
"Before the end of July we are going to come up with the next tranche of about $2.8 million dollar bonds," Asare Akuffo told Reuters.
Structure and yield of seven percent per annum are likely to be the same as for the first issue last September, he said.
That $2 million, five-year dollar-denominated bond issue, the first of its kind in Ghana, was oversubscribed by 25 percent.
"The appetite of the market remained strong. There has been continuous demand for our bonds at the Ghana Stock Exchange but all investors are holding on," Akuffo said.
Ghana Stock Exchange Managing Director Yeboa Amoa described the first issue as "the beginning of the organised medium- to long-term bond market in Ghana."
The instrument's main attraction is that it offers Ghanaians the possibility of hedging against depreciation of the local cedi currency.
The bonds, with a face-value of $100, can be paid for in cedis. A minimum of $1,000 worth must be bought. Bonds may be redeemed after two years.
Last year, HFC indicated its desire to offer further tranches, carrying out a shelf registration for a total of $35 million.
